To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

prompted voiding can be successfully used to improve urinary continence in a significant percentage of incontinent nursing home residents, and that the success of prompted voiding is related to the patient's ability to request assistance.
the use of prompted voiding, with or without bladder training, is an effective treatment of urinary incontinence in the nursing home population.

1) prompted voiding is a highly effective nursing intervention for the management of urinary incontinence in geriatric inpatients; 2) the success rate is highest when patients are motivated, and when they have normal bladder capacities and normal residual urine volumes; and 3) patients with abnormal bladder capacities and residual urine volumes do not respond well, and may require more intensive nursing or medical management.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an intervention to improve the quality of care of incontinent residents in nursing homes.
the development and evaluation of an innovative, non-pharmacologic approach to incontinence in the elderly nursing home population.
the identification of a group of geriatric inpatients that can be managed with nursing interventions alone, without resorting to the use of drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
prompted voiding is a useful technique that improves the quality of life in many nursing home residents.
the nursing management of urinary incontinence can have a positive effect on the quality of life for many geriatric nursing home patients.
the use of prompted voiding, with a specific toileting schedule, is an excellent nursing management technique for incontinent nursing home patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
prompted voiding is a safe and effective nursing management procedure that should be used routinely in the care of geriatric incontinence.
the nursing management of urinary incontinence is an important and effective component of the care of the geriatric inpatients in long-term care.
, for the majority of patients, the most effective way to manage urinary incontinence in the nursing home setting is to use a nursing management approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in a large percentage of geriatric inpatients, incontinence is not an unavoidable consequence of aging, and can be reversed through nursing management procedures.
nursing management is an important part of the treatment of incontinence in the inpatient nursing home population.
the majority of patients can be helped with nursing management techniques.
